messages.subject: corenv() taking a very long time!
messages.subject_clean: corenv() taking a very long time!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm new here; an evolutionary biology graduate student studying wren song degradation. I've been trying to use the corenv() command but keep running into a problem where the command takes ages to run (2-3 hours). Seeing as I need to run this command nearly 10,000 times, I need it to be much faster!

When running the example provided by the Seewave website (1 second clips of the file 'orni'), corenv() completes in about one seconds. I have compared my samples with those examples provided and have determined that they are similar in almost every way. I've loaded my sounds in using LoadWave and cut them using cutw() as shown in the example, both are 16 bit, both have the same sampling frequency. My samples are about 2.5 seconds long.

Some things I've tried:

- down sampling (originally tried at f = 48000)
- trying to correlate the same exact wave file
- trying 1 second slices
- using band pass filters
- setting output = Wave and = matrix when using cutw()
- trying both envt = absolute and hilbert
- trying multiple wave files

Hoping for help soon-- my analysis has ground to a halt!

Thanks,
Braelei

messages.subject: Re: corenv() taking a very long time!
messages.subject_clean: corenv() taking a very long time!
messages.body_plain:
After speaking with Jerome Sueur, I was able to solve the problem. My files simply had a lot of samples (nearly 50 times that found in the orni example), so the sheer number of computations took its toll. This was solved by smoothing the amplitude envelope using the argument 'msmooth' within the corenv() function.

Braelei
